posts.title: Why Sound Strategies Stall After the Announcement
posts.excerpt: Announcing a new direction is an event. Building the shared understanding required to execute it across teams is a disciplined communication process.
posts.author: J. Ayo Makinde
posts.featuredImageAlt: Executive leadership strategy and communication advisory session

blocks.content: Across boardrooms and public institutions, leaders invest months refining strategy documents only to watch implementation lose momentum weeks after the launch. The diagnosis is rarely a lack of intelligence or effort. More often, what was clear in the room where the decision was made becomes fragmented as it travels through the organisation.
People do not act on a strategy as it was written. They act on what that strategy means for their role, their priorities and their daily decisions.
Where Meaning Drifts Between Intention and Execution
When senior leaders announce a priority without testing how middle managers and frontline teams interpret it, three predictable gaps emerge:

items: Competing interpretations of what takes precedence over existing work.
Hesitation at handover points where departmental responsibilities overlap.
Delayed feedback when teams encounter practical obstacles on the ground.

blocks.content: Before asking why teams are moving slowly, examine what each layer of the organisation understood the decision to mean.

posts.title: Diagnosing Communication Problems Before Prescribing Solutions
posts.excerpt: When a message fails to land, the instinct is often to speak louder or redesign the campaign. Yet the real issue may be trust, context or weak feedback.
posts.author: J. Ayo Makinde

blocks.content: When organisations experience stakeholder pushback or internal confusion, the default response is frequently tactical: issue another press release, hold another town hall, or commission a new deck. Activity increases, but clarity does not.
Four Diagnostic Questions That Change the Response

items: What did leadership actually intend to achieve?
What did the audience hear and understand based on past experience?
Where did meaning shift along the chain of communication?
What conditions are needed for credible dialogue and action?

blocks.content: By investigating the underlying communication condition first, institutions avoid wasting resources on louder messaging when the true requirement is clearer direction, stronger listening or stakeholder alignment.

posts.title: Translating Complex Policy Reforms into Public Understanding
posts.excerpt: How public institutions, development programmes and journalists can bridge the gap between technical policy language and everyday citizen realities.
posts.author: J. Ayo Makinde
posts.featuredImageAlt: Development communication and media engagement session

blocks.content: Public reforms and development interventions often struggle not because their technical design is flawed, but because the citizens and communities affected by them cannot see how the policy connects to their daily lives.
Technical accuracy and human meaning are not opposites. Public-interest communication succeeds when rigorous evidence is expressed through stories people can recognise and verify.
The Role of Informed Media and Institutional Clarity

When journalists are equipped to interpret sector data and public institutions communicate their mandates transparently, public conversation moves beyond announcements toward informed scrutiny and constructive participation.
